relevance_note: Case report of an ABCA1 compound heterozygote with Tangier disease plus a literature table of 132 earlier cases: 'this patient had compound heterozygosity for V825I and N935T'.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually. Table 1 (132 previously published Tangier disease cases; bare-number first column with an empty header) was transcribed by a short Python script that splits each row into its 11 cells; I checked the parse (132 rows, 11 cells each, sex/symbol/text cells listed and reviewed) and every span is a row prefix from the patient number through the cell. Labels follow 'Table 1 #<n>'. Source reference = the last two cells (author, year) of each row. The unlabeled 'age' column was recorded as age at last evaluation/report (the paper does not say which age it is). Table 1 '+'/'-' symbols are not defined in the legend or text: '+' was read as present (angina; 'other vascular disease'), '-' and blanks as not reported (no exclusions). Angina and 'other vascular disease' were NOT mapped to the checklist items 'coronary artery disease' or 'non-coronary atherosclerotic arterial disease' for Table 1 patients, because the table does not say the disease is coronary/atherosclerotic. Numeric lipid values (e.g. HDL-C 0 mg/dL) were not converted to low/high checklist statuses (no reference range for these patients); only explicit words were used: 'not detectable'/'unmeasurable' HDL-C -> low HDL observed (#79, #120), 'not detectable' LDL-C -> low LDL observed (#79), TG 'increased' -> hypertriglyceridemia observed (#42), TG 'not detectable' recorded as a feature only (#123). Row #76 HDL-C/LDL-C 'absent' was left not reported because 'absent' is ambiguous (could mean data absent). '< 5'-type values left not reported. Table 2 is a group summary (CVD+ n=26 vs CVD- n=41) and gave no individual data. Proband's family history (father, mother with angina pectoris, elder brother with cerebral infarction, younger sister who died of renal failure) was not given rows: none is described as tested or as affected with Tangier disease. Supplemental Table 1 has the proband as its one data column ('Proband'); arrows (↓, ↑) are not defined in the legend, so only text-stated abnormalities were recorded, with table values as detail. Proband label is 'patient' (rule 5); 'the proband' is a role word. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) timing of the Tangier diagnosis: the Abstract places it in the sequence at 46 years ('At 46 years old ... the patient was diagnosed with Tangier disease. At 52 years old, effort angina recurred'), while the Case Presentation places it at the age-52 re-evaluation; age at diagnosis left not reported. (2) The variants are called 'single-nucleotide polymorphisms' in the Abstract but 'compound heterozygosity' and 'N935T is a novel mutation' in the text; pathogenicity recorded per variant from the closest statement (V825I: 'single-nucleotide polymorphisms'; N935T: 'novel mutation'). (3) Text says angina in 33 of 133 cases, but Table 1 has 31 '+' in the angina column (32 with the proband); 'other vascular disease' 29 '+' matches the text's 29. (4) Table 1 rows #53 (Matsuzawa Y et al 1991, 47 M) and #69 (Komuro R et al 2000, 48 M) have identical lipid values (28/6/232) despite the note that the same cases were listed once; possible duplicate, not merged. (5) Abstract says claudication etc. at 53 '15 months after surgery'; case text says 'Thirteen months later, at 53 years old, 1 year after the previous CABG'. Age at death not stated (died during the admission at 53), so deceased_age left null. Variant type not stated (no 'missense'), left not reported; protein-level strings V825I/N935T recorded as printed (no 'p.' prefix). Whether the proband was among earlier reports by the same group (refs 6, 7) is not stated.

Additional analysis revealed two single-nucleotide polymorphisms (V825I and N935T) in the ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) gene
